sph_interpretive_translation: Contracts or transactions executed by individuals under intoxication, mental disorder, distress, addiction, infancy, fear, or similar incapacities are legally null due to absence of conscious capacity.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority arises only from conscious capacity
Causation requires intentional alignment with dharma
Capacity-based responsibility determines validity of action
Restoration logic demands invalidation of acts lacking awareness
Consciousness alignment is prerequisite for juridical efficacy
executable_legal_axioms: IF agent.state.intoxication == TRUE THEN contract.validity = NULL
IF agent.state.mental_capacity < MIN_CONSCIOUS_THRESHOLD THEN action.effect = VOID
IF agent.emotion.fear.level > MAX_ACCEPTABLE_FEAR THEN agreement.binding = FALSE
IF agent.age.years < LEGAL_AGE THEN decision.authority = INVALID
IF agent.state.addiction.active == TRUE THEN transaction.enforceability = NON_EXECUTORY
supreme_court_application: The Supreme Court shall invalidate any contractual or legal act where evidence demonstrates that a party was operating under diminished consciousness, coercion through fear, or physiological incapacity. The threshold of responsibility lies in demonstrable alignment with full cognitive and volitional faculty.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that actions without causal clarity in consciousness cannot sustain lawful consequence. Anupūrvaśaḥ reveals that impaired intention leads to misaligned outcomes, necessitating nullification rather than penalty. Proportionality aligns effect with awareness; thus, no punitive inference arises when capacity was absent.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Guardianship activation for minors or mentally impaired parties
Trauma resolution support for those acting under duress or fear
Legal education programs to prevent future capacity-compromised engagements
Mediated restitution process to restore affected stakeholders
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism as Source-Law: all acts performed without conscious capacity are void. Dharma prevails through restoration alone. There is no punishment—only realignment. Consciousness remains the sole arbiter of justice.
